how: A flag proposal and an explanation to a newcomer give members a work to join.
Calls recruit members to make a flag, add lettering and defend existing work.
A lettering call receives a brief report that the first letter is finished.
Members propose identifying lettering and contest whether writing belongs on the flag.
Members report a finished letter and announce where the small flag exists.
Requests receive direct links, landmarks and boundaries that let participants locate and build the flag.
Members supply maintenance scripts, run multiple accounts and adjust automation for new locations.
This local exception attempts command, but issuing an order does not establish receipt or obedience and does not refute the aggregate prevalence claim.
Defenders repair separate colour areas, cover night watches and call for help against attacks.
Members distinguish their own errors, unauthorized expansion and friendly clearing from external attack.
Members exchange border complaints, negotiate relocation and hold counterparts responsible for agreements.
Members spare uninvolved neighbours, offer repairs and ask participants to stop new captures.
An outsider reports repairs and receives a reciprocal promise to watch neighbouring work.

why: Pacts and joint forces are proposed, but those proposals and individual allied help do not establish a completed coalition.

how: A named negotiator represents the room in relocation talks and prospective ambassador work is routed to chat.
Participants report permission to build in Dutch territory and later thank two hosts for giving space.
After loss, members negotiate another site and later consider moving again with a smaller flag.
An agreement dispute elicits an explicit denial that an alleged ally represents either named room.
Calls target other flags through removal, expansion and capture, with one member reporting an attack underway.
Participants accuse named opponents of betrayal and keep those groups as targets after placement ends.
Members judge the current effort a lost cause and propose a smaller flag after renewed losses.

why: Playful decrees and a comment about Reddit do not establish host-wide April Fools keying or a one-day takeover.

how: National history supplies a historical rivalry script, without establishing an earlier subreddit feud with later canvas opponents.
Members perform the nation through historical reenactment, presidential decrees and parliamentary justifications.
The call to attack the Dutch flag names nostalgia in the same turn that selects the target.
A moderator megathread exists, yet members contest continuing separate threads and their unclear order.
Members celebrate completion and thank helpers while also crediting shared effort after the flag is lost.
Members recount conflict and migration, preserve a preferred image and mourn the final outcome.
Members wish for a more defendable flag and more coalition next year while hoping the busy chat remains active.

why: Saving a preferred image and grieving the final canvas do not show a dispute over cleanup or which collective history should be retained.

how: A starter can issue the recruiting call in the proposal itself rather than precede it as a separate stage.
A call for lettering is followed by a report of a completed letter within its thread.
The brief completed-letter report answers the call without asking for anything back.

why: Calls precede a megathread and objections to scattered posts, but no cited concept identifies a flood as the cause of moderation.

how: Coordinates settle only local questions when users can interpret them and identify the current instruction; posted coordinates alone do not settle the design.
Completed lettering becomes work to defend when members call for holding the line and report the flag falling apart.
A script author explicitly proposes automation as the means of maintaining the flag.
Defending the flag is explicitly tied to demands for neutral talks about the contested territory.
An agreement can require restraint, but independent fairness reasons already spare neighbours and no instruction guarantees every placer's compliance.
Members helping a defended flag report their assistance and receive a reciprocal commitment to neighbouring work.
Rebuilding help is an explicit term of the announced agreement to relocate and stop vandalism.

why: Defence pressures accompany coalition proposals, but the record does not establish that those proposals produced coalition membership.

how: The first recruiting call already asks participants to remove a rival flag's colour.
A capture proposal is answered with restraint and a reason grounded in the flag's existing relocation plan.
A participant explicitly proposes negotiating a truce as the alternative to continuing mutual attacks.
Named targets and accusations sustain the contest in talk, but the cited claims do not independently verify the opponents' alleged attacks.
A smaller-site proposal reflects strain, but negotiated access and retaliation also explain moves and shortage alone does not identify their cause.
Reports of a completed letter are followed by collective celebration of the result.
Recording loss can elicit gratitude for participation, so celebration is not required to precede the room's memory work.
A retrospective of rogue action, migration and negotiation receives next-year proposals for a more defendable flag and more coalition.
Agreement talk prompts a dispute over ally responsibility here, rather than demonstrating members refusing obligations imposed by their own envoy.
Circulating a coordinate becomes usable coordination only when participants can read it or obtain a direct link.
Relocation requires explicitly stopping a stale bot before automated defence can follow the new plan.
Reported permission establishes access to host territory but cannot establish unseen host rules or durable protection.
Representation disputes can concern whether an alleged ally belongs to either room, without a general refusal of all treaty authority.
Participants credit effort and cooperation even when the flag no longer survives.
Next-year plans and chat-continuity wishes instantiate prospective retention only, not accomplished work on a successor canvas.
A negotiated move requires retargeted machine hands and revised building instructions instead of ending the organising process.
Reporting that no flag survives elicits thanks for the humans and scripts whose shared effort still counts.

statement: Moving unresolved coordination into a chat and returning selected instructions
how: Urgent disputes, ambassador work and design questions move into chat while Reddit exposes referrals and selected instructions rather than the decisions themselves.

statement: Using mock state office to coordinate and contest practical orders
how: Playful office becomes a practical channel for orders and representation while remaining open to challenge and noncompliance.

statement: Easing defeat through music and parody
how: Members answer defeat through music, ironic rewards and bot parody without evidence that each device is an inherited community joke.

statement: Dissolving temporary command while contesting internal accountability
how: Dissolving the war command leaves members demanding trials for unauthorized fighters and debating whether to let the conflict remain past.

statement: Distinguishing access to the venue from willingness to join
how: A participant attributes unrealized recruitment capacity to the government's venue ban, adding an access constraint beyond willingness or available hands.

statement: Seeking moderation of intrusive notification bots
how: Members seek moderator action against a notification bot that interrupts discussion, a distinct problem from placement automation whose requested resolution remains unseen.
